exposure: Gestational age at birth (extremely preterm: 23-27 weeks, very preterm: 28-31 weeks, moderately preterm: 32-33 weeks, late preterm: 34-36 weeks, early term: 37-38 weeks, full term: 39-41 weeks, post term: 42-45 weeks)
cohort: The study included 5,501,276 individuals born alive between 1987 and 2016 in Finland, Norway, and Sweden, to mothers whose country of birth was the respective Nordic country.
finding: Individuals born late preterm and early term had an increased risk of type 1 diabetes, while those born extremely preterm or very preterm had a decreased risk, compared with individuals born full term.
followup_time: Individuals were followed from birth (1987-2016) until diagnosis of type 1 diabetes, death, emigration, or end of follow-up (31 December 2016 in Finland, 31 December 2017 in Norway and Sweden), with a maximum follow-up of approximately 30 years.
